best_for: People who keep chat apps open all day and want a free browser with a built-in ad blocker, a no-sign-up VPN for browsing and messengers in a sidebar.

points.title: Ad blocker and VPN in the box
points.text: Opera ships with a free ad blocker and a free VPN, so you skip hunting for extensions. The VPN needs no account or email and has no data cap.

points.title: The free VPN covers the browser only
points.text: The free VPN encrypts Opera's own traffic, not other apps, and offers three server locations: the United States, the Netherlands and Singapore. Whole-device protection with 48 locations is the separate VPN Pro product.

points.title: Messengers live in the sidebar
points.text: WhatsApp, Telegram, Messenger, Discord and Slack can sit in a side panel next to your tabs. Tab Islands group related tabs on their own, and an AI assistant can summarize the page you are on.

points.title: Chrome extensions install
points.text: You can add extensions from the Chrome Web Store with an Add to Opera button, so most of the tools you use in Chrome carry over.

points.title: Sync needs an Opera account
points.text: Bookmarks, history and open tabs sync only when you sign in to an Opera account. You can choose what syncs and add a passphrase that encrypts the synced data.

points.title: Free, but not open source
points.text: The browser costs nothing, but its license is proprietary, unlike Firefox or Chromium.

points.title: Linux runs a step behind here
points.text: The Flathub build is x64 only, is not marked as verified by Flathub, and currently sits at 139 while Windows and Mac have 140. Opera's own site also offers .deb, .rpm and Snap packages.

points.title: Pick your install scope on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing has x86, x64 and Arm64 builds in per-user and all-users forms, and keeps 169 versions. The Mac build is universal and needs macOS 13 or later; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
